cwLineLibraryFeature.summary: The CW Line Library turns the manual measurement-drawing workflow on Comfort Works catalogue photos into a draw-once, replay-forever system. When measurement lines are drawn on an imported CW photo, they are captured as a reusable "recipe" keyed by the photo's catalogue geometry. Any future import of a photo with matching geometry — same cover, any fabric colour — has its lines auto-drawn with the saved labels and centimetre values, exactly as if drawn by hand.

goals.goal: Eliminate repeated manual drawing of the same measurement lines on the same CW product photos.
Work across the entire Comfort Works catalogue: every active product becomes "searchable and already measured" once it has been drawn once.
Handle Shopify's one-product-per-colour duplication so one drawing serves every fabric variant.
Persist recipes across reloads, browsers, and devices.

dataFlow.step: Every stroke committed on a CW-imported photo dispatches openpaint:stroke-created. A debounced listener (1.2s) snapshots all vector line strokes on the view, converts their endpoints to normalized photo coordinates (0..1 relative to the background image via inverse affine transform), and upserts a recipe into the library. The latest drawing always wins: the recipe is replaced wholesale.

Recipes persist to localStorage immediately and are PUT to /api/cw-line-library (debounced 800ms). The server writes a local JSON file in dev and mirrors the library to an R2 object (cw-line-library/v1.json) in production. On startup the client GETs the server library and merges by updatedAt (newer wins per key).

During CW photo import, after the guide seeding step, each selected photo's catalogue URL is looked up in the library. Matching photos are activated one by one (switchView + wait for canvas ready), the recipe is translated back to canvas coordinates, and lines are created through the same code path as manual drawing: fabric.Line + arrowManager.applyArrows + FabricControls.createLineControls + metadataManager.attachMetadata + applyMeasurement + tagManager.createTagForStroke. Matching measurement rows are marked completed so the draw queue skips them.

architecture.geometryKey:
Parsed from the catalogue image filename stem, e.g. IK-TD-2M__L%28VELC_SP%29_STCC_01.png reference = IK-TD-2M styleCode = VELC_SP (from parenthesized group; dash-separated styles also stripped) component = STCC (last all-letter token) sequence = 01
exactKey = "IK-TD-2M|VELC_SP|STCC|01" looseKey = "IK-TD-2M|STCC|01"
Lookup order: exactKey, then looseKey, then scan for any recipe whose looseKey matches. This is what makes one drawing serve every colour and (as fallback) every style of the same cover component. Non-catalogue photos (lifestyle, storefront) fall back to a "stem:" key of the full filename — replayable only for byte-identical URLs.
architecture.recipeShape:
{ "key": "IK-TD-2M|VELC_SP|STCC|01", "looseKey": "IK-TD-2M|STCC|01", "reference": "IK-TD-2M", "styleCode": "VELC_SP", "component": "STCC", "sequence": "01", "imageUrl": "https://img.comfort-works.com/...", "lines": [ { "label": "A", "value": "133", "sourceLabel": "Width (A)", "x1": 0.05, "y1": 0.20, "x2": 0.40, "y2": 0.20 } ], "updatedAt": "2026-09-05T10:00:00.000Z" }
Line endpoints are normalized to the background photo box so recipes replay at any canvas size, zoom, or fit mode.

file.role: Core module: geometry keys, recipe store, capture, replay coordinate math, console bridge (window.cwLineLibrary).
Integration: capture listener on openpaint:stroke-created, replay phase in the Import Photos handler (replayCwLibraryLinesForView, autoDrawTargets), init wiring in initCwImportUI.
GET/PUT /api/cw-line-library — local JSON file fallback (data/cw-line-library.json, gitignored) plus R2 object mirror.
Registers the routes via registerCwLineLibraryRoutes(app, '/api/cw-line-library'). Requires server restart after edits to app.js.
9 unit tests: geometry-key parsing, capture normalization, style-independent lookup, replay round-trip, used-label skipping.

automated.expectation: 9/9 pass. Full suite: npm test (419+ pass; the extension-install-guide version mismatch failure is pre-existing and unrelated).

manual.step: Restart the dev server (npm run dev). Vite auto-spawns Express and proxies /api; the route only exists after a restart.

Capture: open the app, click CW Import, search a product (e.g. Tylosand), import photos, and draw measurement lines manually. About a second after the last stroke the console logs: [CW Line Library] Captured N lines for <geometryKey>.
Verify in DevTools: window.cwLineLibrary.snapshot() returns { recipeCount, lineCount, references }.

Replay: open CW Import again and import the same product's photos. Matching photos auto-draw their lines with labels and values applied; the measurement queue marks them done. The import status ends with "Auto-drew N saved lines across M photos from your line library."
Persistence: reload the page — snapshot() still shows the recipes (localStorage). The server mirror is data/cw-line-library.json; the curl above then reports "source":"local".
Colour independence: import the same cover in a different fabric/style. Lines should still auto-draw via the loose geometry key.
Reset for a clean run: localStorage.removeItem('cwLineLibrary:v1') then window.cwLineLibrary.reload().

troubleshooting.issue: Stale Express child still running. Kill node app.js / restart npm run dev.

issue.symptom: No [CW Line Library] capture log after drawing

troubleshooting.issue: The view is not recognized as a CW-imported scope (no entry in state.importedViewMetaByScope and no seeded cwImportedMeasurementsByImage), or the photo resolved no http catalogue URL. Check console for capture warnings.

issue.symptom: Replay does not fire on import

troubleshooting.issue: The photo's geometry key differs from the captured one. Compare with window.cwLineLibrary.find('<imageUrl>') and inspect the logged keys.
Canvas background was not ready (waitForImportedViewReady timeout) or all labels already existed on the view.

catalogueRollout.coverageModel: The library grows passively: the operator keeps drawing with the existing armed-row workflow, and each completed photo silently becomes a recipe. No extra clicks. Over time the whole active catalogue converges to "search, import, lines already drawn."
catalogueRollout.shopifyProducts:
Authoritative list of active products (user-provided): https://admin.shopify.com/store/comfortworkscovers/products?savedViewId=650899718452
Public, credential-free access to the same catalogue for scripts: https://comfortworkscovers.myshopify.com/products.json?limit=250&page=N (750+ products observed; multiple pages needed)
Known quirk: many covers exist as one Shopify product per fabric+colour (e.g. "Snuggler Dog Bed - Signature Microfiber Dark Coral", "...Coral", "...Forest Green"). The geometry key deliberately ignores fabric and colour, so a single recipe covers the whole colour family of a cover component. Styles (VELC_SP, SHRT_SP, ...) match exactly first and fall back to shared geometry.

knownLimitations.limitation: Only straight lines replay. Curve/path strokes are skipped during capture (they would distort if replayed as lines).
Zippers and text objects are excluded from recipes.
Lifestyle and storefront photos use a filename-stem fallback key: they only replay for byte-identical URLs.
Server persistence is whole-file last-write-wins — fine for single-operator use; concurrent editors on different devices could overwrite each other's newest recipes if R2 is not configured.
Products never drawn before still require one manual session (by design: geometry comes from the operator, not from CW — the CW API exposes measurement values only, no line coordinates).

roadmap.item: Coverage panel in the CW Import dialog: walk the Shopify products.json list, match against library references, and show which active products still need a first drawing (per-product / per-component badges on photo cards: "saved lines" vs "new").

Cold-start pre-placement for never-drawn products using the existing POST /api/measurements/generate pipeline (SAM strategy, Gemini fallback) to suggest line positions the operator only has to verify.
Curve stroke replay (store sampled path points normalized like line endpoints).
Per-key history instead of last-write-wins, if multiple operators run concurrently.
